kab0: Broken or Bruised Ribs: Healing Time and Breathing Exercises | İhsan Eren
kab1: How long do broken or bruised ribs take to heal, and how do you breathe and cough when it hurts? The active cycle of breathing, four exercises and urgent warning signs.
kab3: A fall, a blow to the chest or very severe coughing can break or bruise your ribs. Breathing in and coughing can be very painful, but ribs usually heal on their own. The most important thing during this time is to keep breathing deeply and moving despite the pain: this helps prevent a chest infection.

kab21: Do this cycle, recommended in an NHS leaflet, at least 4 times a day, or more often if you are struggling to clear phlegm. It is best done sitting; you can hold a folded towel or pillow to your chest.
kab22: Relaxed breathing: Rest one hand on your tummy and breathe slowly in and out through your nose until you feel calm.
kab23: Deep breathing: Breathe in deeply enough to feel your ribs expand sideways, hold for 2–3 seconds, then breathe out slowly. Repeat 4 times.
kab25: Huffing: With your mouth open, breathe out long and steadily, as if steaming up a mirror. When phlegm comes up, take a deep breath in and give a short, sharp breath out.
kab26: Supported cough: If you have phlegm, cough while pressing a pillow against the broken area.
kab27: Four exercises to keep your lungs and body moving
kab28: Lying down or staying still for long periods makes recovery harder. Do not strain yourself, do not lift heavy objects and avoid movements that make your pain worse.
kab30: Sit upright with your hands on your lower ribs. Breathe in through your nose deeply enough to feel your ribs expand sideways, hold for 2–3 seconds and breathe out slowly. Time it for when your painkillers are working.
kab31: 4 repetitions, at least 4 times a day
kab33: Coughing with a pillow for support
kab34: When you need to cough, press a pillow or folded towel over the broken area and cough. Do not hold back phlegm: coughing helps prevent a chest infection.
kab37: Now and then during the day, slowly lift your shoulders up and down and roll them backwards. This stops your shoulders and back stiffening; do not push into pain.
kab38: Now and then during the day, a few repetitions
kab39: Do not lie down or stay still for long periods. Walk little and often, indoors or outside, and build up the time gradually without pushing yourself.
kab41: Often not. Ribs cannot be put in a cast or splinted like other bones; broken or bruised, they usually heal on their own. Your doctor may arrange imaging if they suspect your lung or another organ has been affected.
kab42: Why do breathing exercises matter so much?
kab43: Pain can stop you breathing deeply and coughing. If your lungs do not fill properly and phlegm builds up, the risk of a chest infection rises. Regular deep breathing, coughing when needed and staying active help prevent this.
kab44: When can I go back to work and sport?
kab45: Take time off work and rest if you need to. According to an NHS leaflet, avoid heavy lifting and manual work for at least 4 weeks and contact sports for at least 6 weeks. Do not do sport or exercise that makes the pain worse.
kab47: Broken or bruised ribs usually heal in 2–6 weeks; for fractures it is most often 4–6 weeks. A mild ache may remain for a while afterwards. If your pain has not eased within a few weeks, see your doctor.
